Most new parents hear conflicting advice about tummy time… so let’s clear up a few common myths. 👶✨ ❌ Myth: Stop if your baby cries. ✅ Fact: Babies are building strength! Start with short sessions and gradually increase. ❌ Myth: It only counts on the floor. ✅ Fact: Your chest or lap works too, as long as your baby is awake and supervised. ❌ Myth: Babies who enjoy tummy time can sleep on their tummy. ✅ Fact: Tummy time is for awake time only. Always place your baby on their back to sleep. Remember: Every minute of tummy time helps build the muscles your baby needs for rolling, sitting, and crawling. 💬 Comment “GUIDE” and I’ll send you an easy tummy time routine by age (0–6 months). ✨ Tummy time may seem simple, but it’s one of the best activities for your baby’s development. It helps strengthen your little one’s neck, shoulders, arms, and core muscles while preparing them for exciting milestones like rolling over, sitting, and crawling. 💛 Tummy Time Tips: • Start with 2–3 minutes at a time. • Practice 2–3 times a day when your baby is awake and alert. • Use a firm, flat surface. • Stay close and supervise at all times. • Make it fun with songs, toys, or a baby-safe mirror. Every baby develops at their own pace, so don’t worry if your little one doesn’t love tummy time at first. Consistency is key! 👇 How does your baby feel about tummy time? ❤️ Loves it 😅 Cries after a few minutes Save this reel for later and share it with a new parent who might find it helpful! #tummytime #newmom #NewbornCare #babymilestone #babydevelopment

How many wet diapers does your little one have in a day? Share your experience below to help another new mom. 👇 Being a new mom often means wondering if your baby is feeding enough. 🤍 At around 2 months, most babies: ✨ Feed 6–8 times a day ✨ Show hunger cues like sucking on their hands or rooting ✨ Let you know they’re full by slowing down or turning away One of the best ways to know they’re getting enough milk is by watching wet diapers, weight gain, and overall contentment, not by comparing them to another baby. Remember, every baby is unique. Some poop several times a day, while others may only poop once a week—and both can be completely normal if your baby is otherwise well. 💛 If you notice fewer than about 6 wet diapers in 24 hours, a dry mouth, or your baby seems unusually sleepy or difficult to wake for feeds, contact your baby’s healthcare provider. Most diaper rashes aren’t caused by the diaper itself—they happen when delicate baby skin stays in contact with moisture or stool for too long. Here’s what has helped us: 🤍 Change diapers as soon as they’re wet or dirty. 🤍 Clean gently with fragrance-free wipes or warm water. 🤍 Pat the skin dry—don’t rub. 🤍 Give your baby some diaper-free time every day. 🤍 Use a protective barrier cream when needed. Remember: if the rash becomes severe, doesn’t improve within a couple of days, or is accompanied by blisters, pus, or fever, it’s time to speak with your pediatrician. ✨ Save this reel for later and send it to a new parent who might need it.
